title: Floquet Majorana XYZ Codes with Tunable Logical Dynamics
abstract: We construct Floquet codes from the Majorana XYZ subsystem code with local realizations both in qubits and directly in microscopic Majorana modes with lattice size $L\times L$. For a three-step cycle, odd $L$ supports one static logical qubit, whereas even $L$ supports two. For even $L$ with $L=4n+2$, both logical qubits admit time-independent Pauli representatives. For $L=4n$, by contrast, one Pauli of the second logical qubit remains fixed throughout the cycle, while every representative of its conjugate must evolve through the measurement cycle. This distinction follows from a parity-dependent algebraic obstruction and disappears when the cycle is reduced to two steps, which restores a fully static logical pair. Thus, the same encoded logical degree of freedom can be switched between static and partially dynamical forms by the measurement schedule. With one open direction, suitable protocols can be implemented using only local Majorana parity measurements. To our knowledge, this is the first Floquet-code family with both a local qubit representation and a direct microscopic Majorana realization.
summary: This paper develops Floquet quantum error-correcting codes based on the Majorana XYZ subsystem code, demonstrating that the logical properties are highly tunable by modifying the measurement schedule. The authors show that the code can support different types of logical qubits (static vs. dynamical) depending on the lattice size and the measurement cycle, and they provide a first construction realizing this on local Majorana parity measurements.
main_problem: The paper constructs and characterizes Floquet quantum error-correcting codes based on the Majorana XYZ subsystem code, focusing on how logical dynamics depend on the measurement schedule and lattice size.
main_result: The code exhibits parity- and schedule-dependent logical dynamics, allowing the encoded logical degree of freedom to switch between static and partially dynamical forms by adjusting the measurement cycle. Furthermore, it achieves a direct local Majorana realization for even lattice sizes.
method: The authors analyze the evolution of the instantaneous stabilizer group (ISG) under periodic measurements (Floquet cycles) and derive the code parameters by analyzing the algebraic structure of the stabilizer group generated by local parity measurements.
model_or_system: The system is the Majorana XYZ subsystem code realized on an $L 	imes L$ periodic triangular lattice of Majorana modes. The encoding is achieved by implementing the code using a sequence of local parity measurements ($P_x, P_y, P_z$).
key_observables: The number of supported logical qubits ($k_s, k_p$), the code distance ($d$), and the time evolution of Pauli representatives for the logical operators.
important_parameters: Lattice size $L$ (especially its modulo 4 behavior), the measurement cycle length ($T=2$ vs $T=3$), and the parity of $L$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that local Majorana parity measurements are native operations, and the local realization relies on boundary-peeling arguments for even $L$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the static code structure, the three-step measurement protocol using parallelogram operators, and the local Majorana realization on a lattice geometry.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the static code, then analyzing the dynamics under a three-step Floquet cycle, detailing how $L \pmod 4$ dictates the logical structure, and finally establishing the direct local Majorana realization for even $L$ by analyzing the measurement group generators.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the implementation of topological quantum computation using Majorana fermions, which is a central theme in quantum information theory, by providing concrete, physically realizable protocols.
